The first informant lodged a report with the  allegation that by sending a message to update his Pan Card  to make his HDFC Bank account operational, a sum of  Rs.1,00,000/- was debited from his account, the moment he  opened the link given in the said message.

The applicant  was served with a notice under Section 41A on 15 th March,
 2023, as it transpired that the said amount was credited to  the account of the applicant.
4. The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted  that no amount has been credited to the account of the  applicant.

The statement of account maintained by the  applicant with SBI, Digwadih Branch was pressed into  service to show that no such amount was credited to the  account of the applicant from any of the arrested accused.

5. The learned APP, on the other hand, submitted that  there is material to show that same IMPS Number was used  to credit an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- in the account, with  which the applicant has a nexus.
It was further submitted  that there are a number of transactions in the account of  the mother of the applicant.

6. The learned APP, on instructions, submits that the  recharge has occurred in the year 2021-2022.
The Sim cards  which the applicant has recharged might not be connected with  the instant FIR.
However, the applicant is a part of the racket  which has been indulging in online fraud.
Learned APP further  submitted that the IP address matches with that of the applicant.

sentences.text: Prima facie there  does not appear any money trail.
Nor the amount which the first  informant was fraudulently induced to part with, came to be  credited to the account of the applicant.
The offence under  Section 420 of the Penal Code entails punishment which may  extend to seven years.

In these circumstances, since the applicant  has co-operated with the investigation, at this length of time,
 further custodial interrogation of the applicant does not seem to  be warranted.
I am, therefore, impelled to make the order of  interim bail absolute.
